entries.title: Proverbs 25:1
segments: Copied out; here begins the fourth part of the book, containing a selection of proverbs collected and arranged from the writings of Solomon, probably by Hezekiah's command and for his use.  It repeats a number of proverbs that have already appeared.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:2
segments:
To conceal a thing; he manifests his infinite perfections by the unsearchableness of his ways in both nature and providence. 
 
  To search out a matter; they show their qualification for their high office by sagacity in searching out and understanding every thing that concerns the administration of their government.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:3
segments: The heart of kings; their secret counsels.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:4
segments: A vessel for the finer; a vessel of pure silver to reward the finer's labor.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:5
segments: If rulers would have permanent prosperity, they must banish the corrupt from their councils, and surround themselves with righteous men.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:6
segments: Modesty is the road to true preferment.  Those who ambitiously thrust themselves above their true position, will be, in the end, cast down to the lowest place.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:7
segments: Come up hither; see

entries.title: Proverbs 25:8
segments: The wise man will not engage in controversy till he is sure of his ground, and can see his way through it.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:11
segments: Apples of gold in pictures of silver; golden apples embroidered in picture-work of silver.  Some render, Apples of gold in baskets of silver network.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:12
segments: Reproof wisely administered to the wise is most precious in its results.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:13
segments:
Snow; brought from the mountains and used for cooling drinks. 
 
Fidelity in the execution of a trust is a virtue which men are quick to perceive, and ready to reward; the unfaithful man, on the contrary, is with good reason dreaded and shunned, for he is the ruin of all who put confidence in him.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:14
segments: Boasteth himself of a false gift; makes a vain show of liberality, but gives nothing.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:15
segments: Wise discourse, tempered by mildness and forbearance, is a more effectual weapon than implements of war.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:16
segments: Eat so much as is sufficient; make a moderate use of every privilege that falls to your lot--as, for example, a neighbor's hospitality,
--and do not spoil it by excess.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:17
segments: To abuse a neighbor's hospitality is the way to lose it.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:19
segments: Fidelity in the execution of a trust is a virtue which men are quick to perceive, and ready to reward; the unfaithful man, on the contrary, is with good reason dreaded and shunned, for he is the ruin of all who put confidence in him.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:20
segments:
Vinegar upon nitre; Egyptian nitre, which effervesces with an acid, and loses its strength.  The incongruity of singing songs to a heavy heart is illustrated by two comparisons. 
 
An ill-timed act is unseemly, if not offensive.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:22
segments:
Heap coals of fire upon his head; fill him with shame, and thus bring him to repentance. 
 
He who overcomes an enemy by kindness, gains a victory which makes both parties blessed.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:26
segments:
Falling down before the wicked; either voluntarily, from fear or interest; or, falling under his power. 
 
  Troubled--corrupt; spoiled by the trampling of cattle. 
 
When the righteous yield to the wicked, the very fountains of virtue are corrupted.

entries.title: Proverbs 25:28
segments: As a city without walls is exposed to every assault of the enemy, so a spirit without self-government is the prey of every corrupt passion.
